title: cassia occidentalis var. entreriana
intro: Cassia occidentalis var. entreriana, commonly known as the American Senna, is a plant species belonging to the Fabaceae family, which is native to the Americas. The American Senna is known for its laxative properties and has been traditionally used to treat various health issues, including constipation and digestive problems, due to its health benefits in stimulating bowel movements and promoting the elimination of toxins from the body. Its therapeutic actions include acting as a purgative, laxative, and anti-inflammatory agent, which may help alleviate symptoms of various conditions such as dyspepsia, diarrhea, and skin disorders. The bioactive constituents of the American Senna include anthraquinones, such as sennosides A and B, which are responsible for its purgative and laxative effects, as well as other compounds like flavonoids and phenolic acids, which contribute to its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties.
